title: One-person households' struggle for housing: 'It would be much easier as a couple. I feel like I'm being punished twice'
subhead: Some 12 million people live alone in France, and their number continues to rise. The country's housing stock has not kept pace with this trend, exacerbating the impact of the housing crisis on these individuals.

title: 'In France, the unchecked growth of data centers has more in common with the Wild West than with a digital El Dorado'
subhead: After the building permit for a planned data center in the northern Paris suburb of Le Bourget was revoked, suburban departmental head Stéphane Troussel calls for a pause and holding a public debate in the interest of local residents.

title: Ryusuke Hamaguchi, director of 'All of a Sudden': 'I tend to create my works from dialogue'
subhead: The filmmaker drew inspiration from correspondence between a nursing home director and a theater director who faces terminal cancer. True to his discreet nature, Hamaguchi refuses to have his cinema reflect his personal convictions.

title: After wildfires, southwest France's timber sector preps for mass influx of salvageable wood
subhead: About 4 million metric tons of maritime pine are set to enter the market, nearly two-thirds of the region's yearly output. This influx threatens to upend a sector already hit hard by sluggish economic growth and Storm Nils.

'What will we have left if we stop loving summer?': Heatwaves crush France's season of insouciance
subhead: The heatwave continues across France, with nearly the entire country under an orange alert on Thursday. The recurrence of extreme temperatures has taken a toll on morale, dampening the usual carefree spirit of summer, as residents of Le Perreux and Nogent-sur-Marne, in the Paris region, explained.

title: 'It was either exile or prison': An interview with Boris Nadezhdin, Putin opponent who fled to France
subhead: The veteran Russian politician, 63, tried to challenge Vladimir Putin's regime and its war in Ukraine through legal and electoral means. He failed. Facing the threat of arrest, he decided to leave Russia. His interview with Le Monde is his first since arriving in France.

title: 'I can't stand being only breasts. The eyes burn me': Breasts, a tale of men, women and the times
subhead: 'My Breasts and Me' (4/5). Once a symbol of objectifying women, plastic surgery now draws more women practitioners. The #MeToo wave shook up society and patients' expectations have evolved, reshaping boundaries between genders. Le Monde spent weeks behind closed doors in a private breast surgery practice.
